title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The previous page is headed 'Motifs essentiellement abéliens et théorie du corps de classes'. On this page K is a number field, T_K = R_{K/Q} G_m is the Weil restriction, N_{K/Q} : T_K → G_m is the norm, and V_K = Ker N_{K/Q} is the norm-one torus. This gives 1 → V_K → T_K → G_m → 1.

NB. Global units have norm ±1, so E_K ∩ V_K(Q) has index 1 or 2 in E_K. It contains E_{1K}, the units that are totally positive (the 'unités complètes … y compris à l'∞').

Proposition. Let V' = V_K/R be a Q-quotient torus of V_K. The following are equivalent.
(i) The image of the units in V'(Q) is finite, i.e. R ∩ E has finite index in E.
(ii) For some modulus m, the quotient T → T_m = T/\bar{E_m} kills R, i.e. T/R is dominated by T_m. Here \bar{E_m} is the Zariski closure of the units ≡ 1 mod m. These T_m are exactly Serre's tori from 'Abelian l-adic representations', Ch. II.
(iii) V'_R is a compact (R-anisotropic) torus.
(iv) Let L be the largest 'Weilien' (CM) subfield of K and L_0 = L ∩ R its maximal totally real subfield. Then R contains the kernel of V_K → V_L → V_L/Im V_{L_0}, where the first map is N_{K/L}. Equivalently, V' is a quotient of V_L/Im V_{L_0}.

Proof sketch on the page.
- (i) means V' is dominated by V/\bar F for some finite-index subgroup F ⊂ E_1.
- (ii) ⇒ (i) holds because E_m has finite index in E_1.
- (i) ⇒ (ii) is Chevalley's congruence-subgroup theorem for units: every finite-index subgroup of E contains some E_m.
- (i) ⇒ (iii) passes to R. V_R is the norm-one part of R*^{r1} × C*^{r2}. Dirichlet's unit theorem makes the Zariski closure of F in V_R absorb the whole split part, so the quotient is compact.
- The next page proves the key corollary. For K CM with K_0 = K ∩ R, the quotient V_K/V_{K_0} ≅ T_K/T_{K_0} ≅ U^r is compact. V_{K_0} has no nonzero compact quotient, because K_0 ⊗ R ≅ R^r makes it R-split. Finally E_{K_0} has finite index in E_K, since both unit ranks equal r−1. (iv) ⇒ (i) is then deduced from this corollary.

Purpose. The result determines the 'CM part' of the class-field-theoretic tori: the algebraic quotients through which algebraic Hecke characters of type A_0 (Weil's terminology) factor. Here this means the quotients through which the Galois/motivic group of abelian ('essentially abelian', CM-type) motives over K maps. This is the Serre group S_K, and the result is the well-known statement that its infinity type factors through the maximal CM subfield.
errors: The displayed real structure is garbled. V_R is the norm-one subgroup of R*^{r1} × C*^{r2}. Its real points are ≅ R_{>0}^{r1+r2-1} × (sign group, of order 2^{r1-1} when r1>0) × U^{r2}. The written exponent r1+r2 on R* is off by one.
The formula 'V(R) = /F(R)' is left incomplete after a deletion. The intended statement is V'(R) dominated by V_R(R)/\bar F(R).
Notation drifts between V', V'_K and V''_K/R, between T and V, and between E and E_1. These are harmless.
Next page: '[K_0:K]=r' should read [K:K_0] or [K_0:Q]=r. The rank comparison (both r−1) is correct.

ideas.what: Norm-one torus V_K = Ker(R_{K/Q}G_m → G_m) and the tori T_m = T/\bar{E_m} attached to moduli
ideas.modern_name: Serre's tori T_m and S_m; Serre group

ideas.what: Equivalence: finite image of units ⇔ factorization through some T_m (via Chevalley's congruence theorem for units)
ideas.modern_name: Chevalley's theorem on congruence subgroups of units

ideas.what: Quotients of V_K with finite unit image = quotients that are R-anisotropic = quotients of V_L/V_{L_0}, L the maximal CM subfield
ideas.modern_name: Infinity type of A_0 Hecke characters factors through the maximal CM subfield; CM quotient of the Serre torus
ideas.usually_credited_to: Weil (1955), Serre (1968); later Deligne, Milne (CM tori, Serre condition)

missed.claim: Grothendieck places Serre-type class-field tori, and their CM/anisotropic quotients, explicitly inside a programme on 'essentially abelian motives and class field theory'. This anticipates identifying the Serre group with the motivic Galois group of CM motives, later done by Deligne, Langlands, Milne and Shih via the Taniyama group. The mathematics itself is classical, and the dating (1965 to c. 1977) makes priority unclear.
missed.quote: R contient le noyau de l'homomorphisme V_K → V_L → V_L/Im V_{L_0}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical: it documents Grothendieck's own route to the CM-motive/Serre-group link through the real-compactness criterion, which is essentially the 'Serre condition' for CM Mumford–Tate tori.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a correct, careful rederivation of results standard since Weil and Serre (1968). It uses Serre's own notation T_m. The only interest is historical: it situates them within the motivic Galois programme.
transcription_corrections: 'unités complètes [?]' is likely 'unités complètement positives' (totally positive units, including the condition at ∞).
'V(R) = [-V_R(R)-]/F(R)': the intended formula is V'(R) majoré par V_R(R)/\bar F(R).
The bracket near the bottom is better read as '[le système (λ_i)(μ_j) i.e. ... tels que ∏λ_i ∏|μ_j|^2 = 1]'.
'R*(r1+r2)' carries a deletion mark over its exponent.
